The 'SA2' is simply Hotpoint's model series code for this double oven; it doesn't indicate an error code. The element in the fan oven is separate from the one used for grilling, so it's quite common for one to fail while the other still works. 1. ⚠ Stop using this appliance
A burning or hot-plastic smell, smoke, scorching or melting can mean an electrical fault or a fire risk. Stop using it, switch it off and unplug it (or turn it off at the fuse box), and don't run it again — not even as a test — until it has been checked by a qualified engineer. This is no longer just a simple 'part has failed' situation. That smell suggests an electrical connection inside may have overheated or burnt, which can cause the fan oven to stop working but also poses a fire risk. Please do not use the oven for cooking until it has been inspected by a qualified engineer. The grill still works because it uses a different heating element and circuit path, so that part is likely fine, but the fault in the fan oven section needs a professional diagnosis to ensure there isn't damaged wiring or a risk of further overheating. If you are comfortable doing so with the cooker isolated at the mains, you can look at the back of the fan oven element (the circular ring behind the fan) to see if any wires connected to it look melted, blackened, or loose. However, do not attempt to fix this yourself; simply noting what you see can help the engineer. The safest course of action is to book an engineer to check the internal wiring and components.
